entries.title: It's All Our Blood
entries.maker: Pentagram / Harry Pearce for the University of Maryland Art Gallery
entries.format: Commemorative exhibition poster paired with a process film
entries.why: A strong poster reference for building the entire argument around one physical image-making experiment: the page shows how a single red cloud photograph, strict white space, and restrained timing annotations can carry memorial weight without decorative clutter.
entries.implementationFormat: Concept-led photographic poster with restrained annotation and a supporting process film

entries.title: European Design Festival
entries.format: Festival identity system spanning posters, banners, and flags
entries.why: A strong poster-system reference for translating civic urgency into event graphics: the work uses protest rhetoric, hand-drawn declarations, and European-flag fragments to make a design festival feel argumentative rather than merely celebratory.
entries.implementationFormat: Poster-led event identity with supporting banner and flag applications

entries.title: Shakespeare in the Park 2025
entries.maker: Pentagram / Paula Scher for The Public Theater
entries.format: Season-reopening poster system with dynamic digital animations for the Delacorte Theater relaunch
entries.why: A strong poster-system reference because it derives one year's graphic shift from a concrete spatial cue instead of generic seasonal novelty. The campaign turns the Delacorte's circular seating plan into a poster grammar, then layers manipulated house typography and loud color fields so the reopening reads as civic celebration rather than routine theater promotion.
entries.implementationFormat: Poster-led seasonal theater campaign with static print, large-format public posting, and animated digital derivatives

entries.title: Storefront Gala 2025
entries.maker: Pentagram / Natasha Jen for Storefront for Art and Architecture
entries.format: Annual gala poster and event-key-visual system built from WPA poster density, a custom condensed typeface, and venue-derived pattern cues
entries.why: A strong poster-system reference because it turns one dinner venue and one historical poster lineage into a compact graphic grammar. Instead of decorating the gala with generic heritage cues, the case uses WPA-style compression, a purpose-built display face, and one loud checkerboard accent so the event identity reads like a civic poster set with enough specificity to feel earned.
entries.implementationFormat: Poster-led event identity with custom type, venue-derived pattern, and supporting gala collateral

compositions.title: Isolated blood-cloud focal image
compositions.study: The core image is a photograph of a drop of blood hitting water, held alone so the resulting red cloud reads like an atomic blast rather than a collage of symbols.
compositions.reuse: Use one dominant metaphor image when a poster needs immediate symbolic force and should not dilute the concept with secondary illustrations.

compositions.title: High-contrast white memorial field
compositions.study: The project sets the image on a white background, letting the red cloud do nearly all of the emotional work while the surrounding negative space keeps the poster solemn and legible.
compositions.reuse: Use a large unprinted field when the subject matter benefits from silence, pause, or gallery-like framing.

compositions.title: Time-and-place annotation strip
compositions.study: Grey and black type marks the locations and times of the bombings, turning factual metadata into part of the composition instead of a detached caption block.
compositions.reuse: Fold documentary details into the poster grid when context should sharpen the concept without competing with the hero image.

compositions.title: Declarative slogan posters
compositions.study: Statements such as 'Reset to default settings,' 'Make bold statements,' and 'Who draws the line?' are treated as the image itself, giving each poster a blunt verbal hook before any secondary explanation appears.
compositions.reuse: Let a short declarative line occupy the hero position when a poster needs immediate ideological clarity and can rely on typography more than illustration.

compositions.title: European-flag fragments as modular fields
compositions.study: The graphics borrow parts of European flags instead of quoting one nation wholesale, turning familiar stripes and color blocks into a shared but unstable political backdrop.
compositions.reuse: Sample recognizable civic symbols in fragments when a poster should feel public and collective without collapsing into one literal emblem.

compositions.title: Cross-format protest system
compositions.study: The same rough lettering and confrontational statements carry across posters, banners, and flags, so the identity reads like a coordinated demonstration rather than isolated layouts.
compositions.reuse: Build one loud graphic grammar that can survive format changes when an event identity needs street-level cohesion across print surfaces.

compositions.title: Circular poster field borrowed from the venue itself
compositions.study: Pentagram says the 2025 design is circular for the first time, using the concentric rows of seats at the renovated Delacorte as the base visual idea rather than defaulting to a rectangular stage-poster grid.
compositions.reuse: Pull a poster's primary geometry from the venue or event architecture when a reopening or anniversary needs a form that feels earned, not decorative.

compositions.title: House typography stretched into a seasonal one-off voice
compositions.study: The campaign keeps The Public Theater's Knockout-based identity but pushes it into another yearly variation, proving a poster series can stay recognizably branded while still feeling like a new episode.
compositions.reuse: Treat the brand display face as a material to manipulate each season when continuity matters more than inventing a separate poster type system.

compositions.title: Color shapes and type woven into one festive surface
compositions.study: Pentagram describes the posters and digital animations as layered type over shapes, creating a dense tapestry of color that feels celebratory enough for a reopening without relying on illustration or photography.
compositions.reuse: Use overlapping shape fields to turn a text-led poster into a vivid event surface when the message needs energy but the system should stay mostly typographic.

compositions.title: WPA-style density used as the main poster rhythm
compositions.study: Pentagram says the identity channels WPA posters through compressed layouts, blocky rhythms, and typographic density, making the headline field do the persuasive work instead of relying on illustration-heavy scenes.
compositions.reuse: When an event needs civic authority fast, borrow the pressure and density of historical public-information posters rather than building a loose celebratory collage.

compositions.title: Custom condensed typeface becomes the hero image
compositions.study: The team designed a geometric condensed sans serif with angled corners, then used its narrow proportions as a deliberate counterpoint to Storefront's wider institutional lettering.
compositions.reuse: Make the custom display face carry the poster's personality when one-off event graphics need distinction without inventing a separate illustration system.

compositions.title: Venue pattern turns into a festive secondary field
compositions.study: Bright pink type is paired with a red-and-white checkerboard motif lifted from the Oyster Bar tablecloths, tying the gala posters to the room through a simple repeating surface rather than literal architectural drawings.
compositions.reuse: Extract one repeatable pattern from the venue itself when an event poster should feel site-specific but still stay graphic and scalable.

assets.notes: The final poster image came from repeated physical tests with blood, water temperature, and drop height, then a last-frame photograph by Richard Foster.
assets.reuse: Prototype the central image materially when the poster concept depends on texture, unpredictability, or physical truth.

assets.notes: The supporting typography stays grey and black, functioning as factual annotation rather than expressive decoration.
assets.reuse: Keep contextual type subdued when the image carries the emotional peak.

assets.role: supporting evidence of the image-making method
assets.notes: A behind-the-scenes film extends the poster by documenting the path from blood draw to photography studio to printmaking.
assets.reuse: Add process documentation when the making method is part of the poster's meaning and can deepen trust in the concept.

assets.notes: Bold hand-drawn lettering makes the posters feel urgent and human instead of polished or institutional.
assets.reuse: Use imperfect lettering when a poster should signal debate, dissent, or participation rather than corporate neutrality.

assets.role: shared political color and shape system
assets.notes: European-flag elements create a modular palette and geometry that ties the festival to a continental conversation without relying on one badge-like logo lockup.
assets.reuse: Base poster color systems on extracted civic fragments when an event spans multiple countries or publics.

assets.notes: The slogans borrow professional design terminology while also referring to the financial crisis, giving the posters both insider wit and public relevance.
assets.reuse: Write copy that carries two readable meanings when a poster must speak to a field audience and a broader social context at once.

assets.notes: The campaign continues the long-running Shakespeare in the Park tradition of reworking Knockout into a fresh poster expression each year.
assets.reuse: Recast an existing display type family before swapping brands entirely when a recurring poster series needs novelty with continuity.

assets.notes: Circular and layered color fields echo the venue's seating geometry while giving the campaign enough visual amplitude for large-format public posting.
assets.reuse: Use repeated radial or ring-like shapes when a poster needs both structural order and a sense of public spectacle.

assets.notes: The campaign ties the poster language to 'Shakespeare for the City,' letting the reopening read as a public invitation rather than a closed institutional milestone.
assets.reuse: Anchor poster copy to the broader civic reason for the event when the campaign should feel open and communal, not purely promotional.

assets.notes: The bespoke geometric condensed sans serif supplies the posters' density, contrast, and WPA inflection while staying distinct from Storefront's standing identity.
assets.reuse: Commission or adapt one narrow display face when poster copy needs to stack tightly without collapsing into generic condensed defaults.

assets.notes: A red-and-white checkerboard borrowed from the restaurant's tablecloths gives the system a quick environmental recall that can scale from posters to small takeaways like matchbooks.
assets.reuse: Use one venue-derived repeat pattern as a memory device when a poster system needs a secondary texture that is specific but easy to reproduce.

assets.notes: The identity leans on typographic force and stacked gala information instead of a large image library, keeping the posters closer to public-notice graphics than to lifestyle event advertising.
assets.reuse: Let compact information blocks become part of the poster picture when the event message benefits from urgency and graphic economy.

motion.title: Poster-making documentary extension
motion.notes: The accompanying film reframes the poster as a deliberate physical experiment instead of a digitally composited effect.
motion.fallback: If no motion companion exists, preserve the same making-story through still process frames or a concise caption.

motion.title: Animated digital posters keep the same circular grammar
motion.notes: The official Pentagram page explicitly extends the poster system into dynamic digital animations, suggesting that motion is a derivative of the same shape-and-type logic rather than a separate art direction.
motion.fallback: If motion production is limited, keep the same concentric structure and color layering in static posters so the reopening identity still reads as one system.
